reason: Contract Surface Locking bug-class fix / committed-tree-vs-working-tree hash hardening. The patch touches 21 protected files across three of five LawFirm OS repos (Semantic Substrate, Orchestrator, Exception Lake) because the bug class is intrinsically cross-plane: producers write contract_surface_lock.computed_from_commit, consumers must validate against committed Git-tree blob bytes for that exact commit, and test fixtures must not silently substitute working-tree or temp-copy filesystem bytes. Root cause: consumer/fixture code paths could validate mutable working-tree or temp-copy filesystem bytes while the lock provenance claimed committed Git-tree bytes; on Windows with core.autocrlf=true the CRLF working-tree bytes produced an observable false-drift hash (89c2e811209002ffee48c3eafd35c11a3cb8377ad235f4d47796e5a77b3dc659) against the correct committed-tree hash (d8c80c79cb25bb2c61fbaae8791845aac237c084b9ee4cadbc473835d01eddb4) for Substrate commit 99d54c12df665ce8cc4b6639b50ab5d66889610a. Approved scope: (a) Semantic Substrate producer/validator scripts (compute_contract_surface_hash.py, contract_surface.py, update_consumer_contract_surface_locks.py, validate_contract_surface_lock.py, validate_contract_lock_drift_workspace.py, validate_managed_patch_preservation.py, validate_test_artifact_registration.py, discover_test_artifacts.py) plus per-target managed-patch decision records under registry/managed-patch-decisions/; (b) Orchestrator consumer fail-closed hashing (src/lawfirm_os_orchestrator/substrate/contract_lock.py adds _git_object_exists and explicit raise when a contract_surface_lock pins committed Git-tree bytes but substrate_root is not a git checkout or the locked commit is not present in the object database), regenerated contracts.lock.json pinned to substrate HEAD 99d54c12 with surface_sha256 d8c80c79, regression tests (tests/test_contract_surface_git_validation.py, tests/test_contract_surface_locking.py rewritten to use real git fixture, tests/test_classify_exception.py error-message regexes updated, tests/test_cross_repo_contract.py), and ci-test-manifest.json registration of the new regression suite; (c) Exception Lake consumer (src/exceptions_lake_runtime/contract_loader.py with the same fail-closed pin_committed_tree + git_object_exists guards), producer script (scripts/update_contract_lock.py uses git show / git ls-tree only), restored contracts.lock.json (regenerated via scripts/update_contract_lock.py to clear corrupted fixture-state leftover; pinned to substrate HEAD 99d54c12 with surface_sha256 d8c80c79), fixture hardening (tests/conftest.py builds the temp contract repo via shutil.copytree followed by git init + git add + git commit so CRLF is normalised to LF in the fresh blob bytes, and _pinned_contract_lock recomputes the surface hash from the fixture's committed commit so the loader validates against the same committed bytes), tests/test_contract_loader.py, and ci-test-manifest.json registration of the new regression suite. Out of scope, explicitly not staged: workspace-root files (.ci-route-decision.json, .contract-surface-hash.json, .gitignore, HANDOFF_*.md, PRE_CODEX_REPORT_*.md, exports/, temp/), generated/ephemeral folders (.cursor/, .claude/, .pytest-tmp-local/, .pytest-tmp-root/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/), local patch payload folders (LawFirm-os-*-patch/, patches/), backup artifacts (*.contract-surface-backup, *.skill-agent-control-backup, *.bak), any unrelated Skills Registry source edits, and any lock update to the bad working-tree hash 89c2e811209002ffee48c3eafd35c11a3cb8377ad235f4d47796e5a77b3dc659. Safety constraints enforced by code and tests: (1) no semantic canon mutation, (2) no autonomous writes outside the validator/test surface, (3) no production / real client / real matter data introduced, (4) consumers must hash committed Git-tree blob bytes (git ls-tree + git cat-file blob, or git show <commit>:<path>) when computed_from_commit or substrate_repo_commit_sha is present in the lock, (5) consumers must fail closed on missing commit, missing contract surface registry, unsupported hash algorithm, surface_sha256 mismatch, or contract_repo_root not being a git checkout under a committed-tree pin. Rollback plan: revert the three commits in reverse topological order (Exception Lake first, then Orchestrator, then Semantic Substrate); if a partial revert is needed, restoring the prior contracts.lock.json in each consumer repo from HEAD~1 is sufficient because all validators key off the lock; after revert, re-run validate_contract_lock_drift_workspace.py, validate_test_artifact_registration.py, and route_ci_tests.py to confirm a clean baseline.

alternatives_considered: Split the bug-class fix into three independent per-repo commits applied in separate sessions. Rejected because the bug is a cross-plane contract between producer provenance (substrate writes computed_from_commit) and consumer validation (orchestrator and exception-lake each validate it). A split would leave at least one consumer running mutable-filesystem-byte validation against a committed-tree pin between sessions, which is exactly the bug class being fixed; one round-trip on Windows during the interim could regress lock state and force a second round of work.

Change consumer locks to the observed working-tree hash 89c2e811209002ffee48c3eafd35c11a3cb8377ad235f4d47796e5a77b3dc659 to make Windows tests appear to pass without touching consumer code. Rejected and explicitly forbidden by the user prompt: that hash demonstrably comes from mutable filesystem/temp-copy bytes, not from any committed Semantic Substrate tree (the canonical compute for the locked commit yields d8c80c79cb25bb2c61fbaae8791845aac237c084b9ee4cadbc473835d01eddb4), so accepting it would lock the bug class in place permanently.

Refresh the consumer locks to substrate HEAD blindly via a different commit. Rejected because the user prompt explicitly says 'do not refresh locks blindly'; the only lock regeneration performed in this session was Exception Lake's contracts.lock.json, which was already in a CORRUPTED state pointing to a synthetic fixture commit that does not exist in substrate git history, and was regenerated via the repo's own committed-tree-only producer script scripts/update_contract_lock.py against substrate HEAD 99d54c12 to restore a coherent state. The resulting surface_sha256 d8c80c79 exactly matches both the canonical Semantic Substrate compute and the Orchestrator's pre-existing lock for the same commit, confirming the regeneration is not a blind workaround.

Rollback path (kept on file): revert the three commits in reverse topological order — first the Exception Lake commit, then the Orchestrator commit, then the Semantic Substrate commit — restoring each repo's prior contracts.lock.json from HEAD~1 if a partial revert is required; then re-run validate_contract_lock_drift_workspace.py, validate_test_artifact_registration.py, and route_ci_tests.py to confirm baseline.
